outcomes.text: Choose punctuation from the structure of the whole written sentence.
Set off supplements, parenthetical material and direct speech using a consistent style.
Handle apostrophes, hyphens and terminal punctuation in common editing cases.

key_terms.definition: A mark such as a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark that can end a written sentence.
An expression naming the person being addressed, as in Jo, close the door.
An expression such as however that links a clause’s meaning to surrounding text.
The larger sentence containing an embedded question, quotation or other construction.

options.feedback: The main clause reports a question. The sentence as a whole is a statement.
The main clause reports a question. The sentence as a whole is a statement.
The main clause reports a question. The sentence as a whole is a statement.

opening.prompt: Choose the ending for the report “Mara asked whether the hall was open___”

options.feedback: Mara is the person addressed in the command. The other commas interrupt ordinary connections.
Mara is the person addressed in the command. The other commas interrupt ordinary connections.

options.text: The gate near Mara, is closed.
options.feedback: Mara is the person addressed in the command. The other commas interrupt ordinary connections.

opening.prompt: Which line uses a comma for direct address?

options.feedback: The abbreviation’s final full stop also supplies the visible end of the statement.
The abbreviation’s final full stop also supplies the visible end of the statement.

opening.prompt: How many consecutive full stops follow the final C in the statement “The office is in Washington, D.C.”?

options.text: The hall: by the old entrance was closed.
options.feedback: The second clause explains the closure. A coordinate list of clauses needs a different boundary pattern.

options.text: The hall was closed: the caretaker had gone home.
options.feedback: The second clause explains the closure. A coordinate list of clauses needs a different boundary pattern.

options.text: The hall opened at nine: the clinic opened at ten: the store opened at eleven.
options.feedback: The second clause explains the closure. A coordinate list of clauses needs a different boundary pattern.

opening.prompt: Which line uses a colon to introduce an explanation?

options.text: The gate, as you may recall was locked.
options.feedback: Paired commas enclose the parenthetical material. A long subject alone needs no comma before was.

options.text: The gate, as you may recall, was locked.
options.feedback: Paired commas enclose the parenthetical material. A long subject alone needs no comma before was.

options.text: The gate near the hall, was locked.
options.feedback: Paired commas enclose the parenthetical material. A long subject alone needs no comma before was.

opening.prompt: Which sentence sets off the interruption while keeping the subject with its predicate?

options.feedback: The omission mark has the shape of a closing single quotation mark.
The omission mark has the shape of a closing single quotation mark.

closing.prompt: Which directional apostrophe indicates the missing letters before n in rock ’n’ roll?

options.feedback: Read the parenthesised words too. Unusually immediately follows the article in speech and begins with a vowel sound.
Read the parenthesised words too. Unusually immediately follows the article in speech and begins with a vowel sound.

closing.prompt: Which article fits before “(unusually detailed) manual” when the whole phrase is read aloud?

options.text: Mara said, “The hall is closed.” And turned the key.
options.feedback: The matrix sentence continues after the quotation, so the quoted full stop is dropped there.

options.text: Mara said, “The hall is closed” and turned the key.
options.feedback: The matrix sentence continues after the quotation, so the quoted full stop is dropped there.

options.text: Mara said, “The hall is closed.” and turned the key.
options.feedback: The matrix sentence continues after the quotation, so the quoted full stop is dropped there.

closing.prompt: Which version avoids a quoted full stop inside a continuing sentence?

options.feedback: The internal question mark is retained and the external full stop is suppressed.
The internal question mark is retained and the external full stop is suppressed.
The internal question mark is retained and the external full stop is suppressed.

closing.prompt: A quoted question ends the report “Mara asked, ‘Is the hall open?’” What follows the closing quotation mark?

options.text: the hall’s door / a two-day closure
options.feedback: The genitive takes an apostrophe and the pre-head measure compound takes a hyphen with singular day.

options.text: the hall’s door / a two-days closure
options.feedback: The genitive takes an apostrophe and the pre-head measure compound takes a hyphen with singular day.

options.text: the halls door / a two day closure
options.feedback: The genitive takes an apostrophe and the pre-head measure compound takes a hyphen with singular day.

closing.prompt: Which pair uses the usual word punctuation in both phrases?
